home.title: PolymCrystRefine
home.subtitle: Polymer Crystal Refinement · Data Processing Module · Aux
home.aboutBody: PolymCrystRefine-aux (the PRE auxiliary edition) is a graphical desktop application built to assist the PolymCrystRefine refinement pipeline: from 2D WAXS integration and merged-intensity extraction, through OPLSAA force-field extraction and refinement input generation, to CIF parsing with hydrogen addition, space-group detection and single/dual-phase fiber diffraction simulation — plus DFT-side helpers such as the diffraction-section generator of our CP2K plugin and structure deviation analysis — covering the complete workflow from raw detector images to refined structures and on to DFT optimization.

integration.title: 2D Intensity Integration
integration.desc: pyFAI / PONI-based 2D intensity integration and masking with batch image support.

waxs.title: 2D Integration Processing
waxs.desc: Batch-import images, merge integration results and export 1D WAXS curves.

giwaxs.title: GIWAXS Fiber Integration Merge
giwaxs.desc: Per-image rot3 fiber integration → pixel-wise merge on a shared grid; exports npy / processing_info / PNG.

xrd.title: Diffraction Simulation
xrd.desc: Gaussian-peak XRD pattern simulation with adjustable peak position, FWHM and intensity.

cif.title: CIF Structure Parser
cif.desc: Parse a CIF to generate theoretical fiber diffraction peaks (with azimuth ψ) and export peak_result.txt for the simulator.

analysis.title: Intensity Extraction
analysis.desc: Box-select ROIs on the 2D cake to extract and export integrated intensities, with Miller-index matching.

viewer.title: 2D Integration Image Export
viewer.desc: Load and export 2D integration (cake) images in multiple formats.

inputGen.title: Refine Input Generator
inputGen.desc: Build the complete input.txt configuration for the Fortran refinement engine — fill in all parameters, preview and download.

lmpExtractor.title: OPLSAA Force Field Extractor
lmpExtractor.desc: Upload a structure (PDB/MOL/GRO etc.) + LAMMPS (OPLSAA) data file, check element/mass correspondence, and extract force field parameters as CSV via an old→new atom-ID map.

qzSlice.title: qz Band Integration
qzSlice.desc: Slice a GIWAXS fiber-merge map into qz bands (centers at n×qz, width 2×interval), average each band into an I(q∥) curve, and preview the bands as gray overlays.

cifH.title: CIF Hydrogenation
cifH.desc: Perceive polymer bonds under PBC, add hydrogens to fill every valence, fix bonds interactively in 3D, and export a CP2K-ready CIF.

cp2k.title: CP2K Diffraction Section
cp2k.desc: Generate the &FIBER_DIFFRACTION fiber-diffraction bias section for our custom CP2K-Polymcryst-Refine (v1.1) — diffraction part only; paste it inside &FORCE_EVAL of your CP2K input.

symmetry.title: Space Group Detection
symmetry.desc: Identify the space group with the cell kept unchanged: number, H-M symbol, symmetry operations and asymmetric units, exportable.

deviation.title: Structure Deviation Report
deviation.desc: Compare a DFT-relaxed structure (CIF / CP2K PDB) against the reference: per-atom deviations, average and maximum deviation and cell changes, exportable as Markdown / CSV.

cp2k.title: CP2K Diffraction Section
cp2k.desc: Generate the &FIBER_DIFFRACTION fiber-diffraction bias section for our CP2K-Polymcryst-Refine; paste it into &FORCE_EVAL to optimize.

cifH.title: CIF Hydrogenation
cifH.desc: Perceive polymer bonds under PBC, add hydrogens to fill every valence, edit bonds in 3D, and export a CP2K-ready CIF.

notices.title: Force field: OPLSAA (LigParGen recommended)
notices.body: This tool mainly handles OPLSAA force fields (LAMMPS data format). We recommend generating your files with LigParGen (Yale University): upload your small molecule there, choose the OPLSAA force field, and download the .gro structure file plus the LAMMPS force field file (.lmp / .data), then upload both here.
notices.link: Get .gro + LAMMPS force field files from LigParGen

descs.upload: Upload a structure file (PDB, MOL, SDF, XYZ, CIF, or GRO) and a LAMMPS data file (.data / .lmp). The tool checks that the element/mass composition of both matches.
descs.viewer: Ball-and-stick view of the uploaded molecule. Each atom is labelled with its number; click an atom to toggle its assignment (red ring = assigned). Bonds are recomputed from distances (the file-internal Bonds section is NOT used, so periodic-image bonds don't render as tangled long lines); atoms in a periodic interaction get a cyan ring.
descs.mapping: Assign each atom a new ID column-by-column (Old ID → New ID); leave New ID blank to skip an atom. "Auto sequence" (1 / 2 / -1 markers) numbers the intermediate atoms along the bonded chain automatically. The "Period" column is an integer: 0 = non-periodic, ≥1 = the atom spans N periodic images (seeded from the LAMMPS topology # marker, editable).

hints.bondsAuto: Bonds auto-detected from distances (recomputed each upload)
hints.periodicTip: The "Period" column is an integer: 0 = non-periodic, ≥1 = spans N periodic images. It is written into the topology output (e.g. newID#N); records where every atom is periodic (>0) are skipped on extract.
hints.periodicToggle: Period count (integer: 0 = non-periodic, ≥1 = spans N periodic images)
hints.periodicFile: LAMMPS file detected periodicity — click to additionally set a manual flag
hints.periodicFileN: LAMMPS file detected {n} period(s) for this atom — editable here
hints.noCompare: (structure or LAMMPS missing element info — no comparison)
hints.autoSeqHelp: Auto sequence usage: mark the chain first — enter 1 as the New ID of the start atom, 2 on the second atom (direction), and -1 on the end atom, then click "Auto sequence". The tool numbers the intermediate atoms along the bonded path; the -1 atom receives the final number. Atoms off the chain stay blank for you to choose manually.
hints.autoSeqOk: Auto sequence done: {n} chain atoms, {total} atoms numbered in total ({h} hydrogens).
hints.autoSeqViaH: Note: the chain path passes through hydrogen atoms — please double-check.
hints.autoSeqErrMark: Mark three atoms first: New ID = 1 (start), 2 (second atom), and -1 (end), then click "Auto sequence".
hints.autoSeqErrDup: The 1, 2 and -1 markers must be on three different atoms.
hints.autoSeqErrPath: No bonded path from the atom marked 2 to the atom marked -1 — check your markers or the structure.
hints.negIdWarn: Negative New IDs present (-1 is the end marker): run "Auto sequence" or fix them manually before extracting.
hints.floatTip: In float mode the 3D structure stays pinned in a corner and can be dragged by its title bar — handy for consulting it while picking atoms in the table below.

descs.basic: Core parameters required by the Fortran refinement engine: wavelength, generation count, atom count, and diffraction intensity weight.
descs.coordinate: Define the asymmetric-unit atoms: element symbol, r random range, and z position index. Row count must match num_atoms.
descs.cell: Unit-cell parameters a, b, c (Å) and α, β, γ (°). Note: actual c is determined by z_add × period_num during refinement.
descs.chains: Chain count, space-group symmetry operations, chain centres, and symmetry operators.
descs.helix: Period count, helix number, adjacent-period rotation angle, and Python-side build parameters (required for init-helix / GA).
descs.pythonBuild: Required by the Python init-helix and GA pipeline: per-period z range, expected full-period c-axis length, and main-chain monomer count.
descs.thermal: Temperature (B) factor settings: isotropic only (anisotropic not yet implemented).
descs.lm: Levenberg-Marquardt optimizer settings. Keep status_LM = NO for most workflows.
descs.modes: Mode switches controlling single-chain construction, X-ray source type, stable z, and mirror chain.
descs.phase2: Independent chains and pseudo-symmetry: n_independent_chains, theta_ini_map, build_order, pseudo_symmetry_mode.
descs.experimental: Absorption / air-scatter corrections, HKL indexing range, low-q filter, and background contribution.
descs.ga: Genetic Algorithm configuration: mode (basic/flash/pro), step count, and output directory.
descs.output: Output verbosity level and optional chemical formula. Generate preview and download input.txt.
descs.equatorial: Equatorial (l=0) enhancements [260814]: option 1 sets a separate weight for l=0 blank reflections (replaces blank_contribution); option 2 enables a 1D Rietveld-like profile fit (activated by the profile file). All optional — omit for fully legacy behaviour.
descs.advanced: Advanced multi-molecule mode [260815]: two independent molecular entities in one cell (case_a fixed positions / case_b shared-position 3-domain mixture). Edit molecule coordinates & forcefields in the Coordinate section; chain_num is implied as 2 and not emitted.
descs.chainsAdvanced: In advanced mode chain_num is implied (fixed 2) and must NOT appear; chain centers are still used (case_a one center per molecule, case_b shared). P1 only (space_group_num = 0).

hints.noAtoms: No atoms defined. Click '+ Add Atom' to start.
hints.xraylibAuto: xraylib = on: molecular_mass / sample_absorption_coeff / air_absorption_coeff are auto-derived from composition + wavelength (not emitted); chemical_formula is required (repeat-unit formula).
hints.advancedNote: Advanced-mode conventions: chain_num must not appear (fixed 2); single_chain_mod / stable_z_chain / mirror_chain / build_order must be 0; P1 only; theta bucket & pseudo-symmetry disabled; GA supports basic / flash only (pro → error stop). Position 2 = mirrored placement of position 1 (antiparallel stacking, θ→−θ, z→−z). One forcefield file per molecule (forcefield.txt no longer needed).
hints.numAtomsAdvanced: In advanced mode this is auto-set to the sum of both molecule blocks and ignored
hints.advGaNote: Advanced mode supports GA basic / flash only; pro → error stop
hints.deepSearchNote: Only available with ga_mode=basic, chain_num=2, stable_z_chain=0 and standard mode; splits the best structure into a case_a dual-molecule refinement, archived to result/deepsearch/
hints.cellMissing: Unit cell incomplete: fill all 6 values (a b c alpha beta gamma), or use paste-to-fill
hints.cellLenPositive: Cell lengths a, b, c must be > 0
hints.cellAngleRange: Cell angles alpha, beta, gamma must lie in 0-180 degrees
hints.coordCountMismatch: coordinate rows ({n}) != num_atoms ({total}) - fix before generating
hints.molCoordEmpty: In advanced mode both molecule coordinate blocks need at least one row
hints.advNoSpaceGroup: Space groups are not supported in advanced multi-molecule mode (V1: P1 only); pasted ops were ignored

paste.coordTitle: Paste to fill (you can copy directly from an existing input.txt)
paste.coordPlaceholder:
One atom per line: element r_min r_max z_idx
Example:
O 0 2 1
C 0 1 1
H 0 2 3
(A num_atoms = 22 line is accepted and syncs the atom count)
paste.chainsTitle: Paste to fill (copy a fragment from an existing input.txt)
paste.chainsPlaceholder:
Supports chain_center / space_group blocks, e.g.:
chain_center_begin
0.0 0.0 0.0
chain_center_end
space_group_begin
-1 -1 1
0.25 0.25 0
space_group_end
Without markers: 3 numbers per line = chain center; 6 numbers = one symmetry op (Transdirect + center_move).
chain_num = / space_group_num = lines are applied too.
paste.cellPlaceholder:
Paste 6 numbers: a b c alpha beta gamma
Example:
5.9897 4.5159 10.7076 61.9291 121.3998 113.4930
paste.parsedChains: Parse done: {c} chain center(s), {o} symmetry op(s)
paste.errCoordCols: each row needs 4 columns (element r_min r_max z_idx); this row has {n}
paste.errCoordElement: column 1 must be an element symbol, not a number
paste.errChainsCols: each row needs 3 numbers (chain center) or 6 numbers (symmetry op); this row has {n}
paste.errCellCount: cell needs exactly 6 numbers (a b c alpha beta gamma); got {n}
paste.errNum: contains a value that cannot be parsed as a number

help.generation_num: Population / generation count, must be > 0; also the block count of output.rphi
help.num_atoms: Atoms per asymmetric unit; must match the coordinate row count
help.intensity_contribution: Diffraction residual weight; 0 = ignore diffraction data entirely, typically a positive number (e.g. 400)
help.z_min: Per-period z random range lower bound (A); required by init-helix / GA
help.z_max: Per-period z random range upper bound (A); required by init-helix / GA
help.c_length: Expected full-period c-axis length (A); required by init-helix / GA
help.main_chain_num: Main-chain monomer count, used to scale z onto each atom
help.temperature_factor_stat: B-factor type: 0 = isotropic (the only supported value)
help.temperature_factor_max: B-factor upper bound; falls back to 0.10-0.35 if below the minimum
help.status_LM: Enable LM override settings; NO = tol / maxcall are ignored
help.tol: LM convergence tolerance (only when LM = YES, default 1e-3)
help.maxcall: LM max iterations (only when LM = YES, default 500)
help.period_num: Period count, must be > 0; actual c = z_add x period_num
help.single_chain_mod: Build single chain in inversion-center mode (0/1)
help.xray_source_mod: X-ray source: 0 = synchrotron, 1 = lab source, 2 = polarization factor 1
help.stable_z_chain: 1 = force all z_ini to 0; also changes the rphi header format
help.mirror_chain: Chain mirror mode (0/1/2); auto 0 with a warning when chain_num >= 2 and unset
help.chain_num: Helical chain count, must be > 0; must match the chain-center row count
help.space_group_num: Number of non-identity symmetry ops; > 0 requires the ops table below
help.pseudo_symmetry_mode: Pseudo-symmetry: 0 off, 1 pass-through, 2 bc mirror, 3 ac mirror (>1 needs gating)
help.n_independent_chains: Independent theta_ini parameters (1..chain_num); < chain_num requires theta_ini_map
help.build_order: Build order: 0 = position then symmetry, 1 = symmetry then position
help.use_xraylib: on = mu/rho, M_cell and f0 computed by xraylib from composition + wavelength; off = legacy values
help.chemical_formula: Repeat-unit formula (e.g. C4H10O2); required when use_xraylib = on
help.molecular_mass: Whole-cell mass (g/mol); auto-derived when xraylib on and unset
help.max_hkl_per_peak: Max HKL count per diffraction peak (> 0)
help.max_blank_hkl: Max HKL count for blank reflections (> 0)
help.q_min: Low-q filter threshold; 0 = off, > 0 drops points with q < q_min
help.equatorial_module_on: Off by default; equatorial_* keys are only written when enabled (unset = legacy behavior)
help.equatorial_blank_contribution: Separate weight for l=0 blank reflections; unset = follow blank_contribution
help.equatorial_profile_file: Equatorial 1D observed profile file (workdir-relative); empty = profile fitting off
help.equatorial_profile_contribution: Profile residual weight (independent scaling, not multiplied by intensity_contribution)
help.equatorial_peak_fwhm: pseudo-Voigt peak FWHM (q units A^-1, default 0.04)
help.equatorial_background: Constant background (same units as the curve; subtract background first and keep 0)
help.equatorial_h_max: hk0 enumeration h limit; unset = follow h_max
help.equatorial_k_max: hk0 enumeration k limit; unset = follow k_max
help.advanced_multi_molecule: off = standard; case_a = fixed positions; case_b = shared positions 3-domain mixture (default off)
help.data_param_ratio_warn: Info/parameter ratio red-line (must be > 1; hard gate 1 is fixed)
help.axis_penalty_weight: Axial-offset penalty weight (0 = off; try 1.0 first)
help.mixture_fractions: case_b fractions p1 p2 p12, each > 0 summing to 1; empty = random init
help.mixture_fractions_fixed: yes = fractions fixed during LM (requires explicit fractions)
help.forcefield: Forcefield file name for this molecule (e.g. forcefield_mol1.txt)
help.ga_mode: GA mode: basic default / flash speed-first / pro exploration-first (advanced mode: basic/flash only)
help.deep_search: After the basic loop, split the best structure into a case_a dual-molecule refinement (default off)
help.freeze_streak_k: Freeze after K consecutive stable generations (skip LM)
help.warmup_percent: Warmup fraction of total steps (energy-only optimization)
help.pro_max_age: Max survival generations for aggressive-pool candidates
help.cell_c: Cell edge c (A, > 0, required; actual c comes from z_add x period_num)

integration.title: 2D Intensity Integration
integration.header: pyFAI / PONI-based 2D intensity integration and masking

detector.title: Raw Image + PONI
detector.desc: Upload raw image(s) and a PONI calibration file; pyFAI integrate2d_ng performs azimuthal integration. Multiple images can be imported and integrated in batch.
detector.poniLabel: Drop a PONI calibration file here (.poni)

cake.title: Pre-integrated Cake (.npy)
cake.desc: Process a pre-integrated 2D cake (azimuth × q) directly — masking only.
cake.infoApplied: Axis ranges applied from NPY info file
cake.infoError: Failed to parse NPY info file
cake.infoEmpty: NPY info file contained no recognizable axis ranges

mask.title: Mask Settings
mask.desc: Threshold-based masking with an optional custom mask. Pixels below the minimum or above the maximum are masked.

status.exportedBatch: Exported {n} results (flat ZIP, shared q/chi axes).
status.needInput: Please upload an image file first.
status.needPoni: Raw image mode requires a PONI file.

batchImport.title: Batch Import
batchImport.desc: Drop already-integrated cakes (.npy) or detector images (.tif/.tiff/.edf/.h5) to batch-upload them. Optionally import a single NPY info file (.json or legacy .txt) as axis/parameter info shared by all files — used for display, alignment interpolation and round-trip on export.
batchImport.jsonLabel: Drop NPY info file here (single file, .json / .txt)
batchImport.infoEmpty: ⚠ Read {file} but no recognized fields (expected xAxisRange / yAxisRangeDeg / integrationPoints). Check the file format.

background.title: Background Subtraction
background.desc: Rolling-ball background subtraction applied to each imported cake to remove amorphous halo, air scatter and other slowly-varying backgrounds. Subtracted results can be used as the merge input (toggle in the Merge step).
background.maskZeros: Mask zeros (ignore zero-valued pixels during background estimation)
background.needImport: Upload files in Batch Import first.
background.done: ✅ Subtracted {n} image(s); results are the default merge input (toggle in the Merge step).
background.useMergeForBg: Use merge result as background input
background.mergeNotRun: No merge run yet — background will use original data (per-image).

merge.title: Merge
merge.desc: Align and merge multiple cakes by interpolating onto a common q axis derived from the xAxisRange in the imported NPY info file. Import NPY info file (.json/.txt) to enable q-axis alignment; otherwise a chi-shift merge is used. A per-image chi offset can be set for each cake.
merge.maskLowerBoundHelp: Pixels below this bound (and non-finite pixels) never contribute to the merge; pixels invalid in every input are filled with (bound − 1). In sequential mode each pixel keeps the first valid value.
merge.useBgForMerge: Use background-subtracted results (per-image) as merge input
merge.bgNotRun: Background subtraction not run yet — merge will use original data.
merge.needImport: Upload files in Batch Import first.

giwaxs.title: GIWAXS Fiber Integration Merge
giwaxs.header: Integrate several raw detector images with pyFAI fiber (grazing-incidence) integration — each with its own rot3 override (rot1/rot2 always inherit the PONI) — onto one shared (in-plane, out-of-plane) grid, then merge them pixel-wise into a single fiber-corrected GIWAXS map and export npy + processing_info (optionally with a PNG).

data.title: Data & Calibration
data.desc: Upload several raw detector images and one PONI calibration file; an optional custom mask (nonzero = masked) is supported. The PONI beam center (poni1/poni2 → pixel coordinates) and rotations act as the inherited defaults for the per-image rot overrides.

rot.title: Per-image rot3 settings
rot.desc: Detector rotation about the beam axis (rot3, degrees) for each image. Leave a field empty to inherit the PONI file value; rot1/rot2 always inherit the PONI. Every image is integrated onto the same (in-plane, out-of-plane) grid before merging — the essential difference from the 2D integration processing's integrate-then-stitch flow.
rot.name: File
rot.batchHint: Image i (0-based) gets rot3 = start + i × step. E.g. start 0, step 5, 4 images → 0, 5, 10, 15; step 0 fills the same value everywhere.

integ.title: Integration Parameters
integ.autoRangeHint: Auto mode: the first successfully integrated image fixes the shared (in-plane, out-of-plane) range; all images are integrated onto that grid so the axes are identical.

merge.title: Merge Settings
merge.desc: Same merge semantics as the 2D integration processing: pixel-wise merge of aligned maps. NaN (no-data bins) never contributes.
merge.maskLowerBoundHelp: Pixels below this value (and non-finite ones) do not contribute; pixels with no valid contribution stay NaN (no data). Sequential mode takes the first valid value per pixel.

status.empty: Upload images and a PONI, then click 'Integrate & Merge'
status.runningLog: ▶ Start: {n} images · {npt}×{npt} grid · fiber integration → merge…

cif.title: CIF Structure Parser
cif.desc: Parse a CIF (Crystallographic Information File) and, via pymatgen, generate theoretical fiber diffraction peaks with Miller indices, q and azimuth ψ. Export peak_result.txt for the diffraction simulator.
cif.maxQHelp: Keep only peaks with q at or below this value; leave empty for no limit.
cif.needCif: Please upload a CIF file first.

single.title: Single Phase Fiber Diffraction
single.desc: Simulate fiber diffraction from a peak_result.txt peak list (h k l q psi intensity). Choose Cake mode (azimuth χ vs. q, the original detector representation) or 2D Detector mode (a real pixel-space image via PONI geometry). Fiber four-fold symmetry can be expanded.
single.symmetryHelp: On by default. Each peak is mirrored to all four quadrants (4-fold symmetry), multiplying the peak count by 4; turn it off to show the original quadrant only, which is faster.
single.uploadPeakResult: Upload peak_result.txt (generate & download it from the CIF Structure Parser)

result.cropHint: Box-select on the image to crop the view

cake.title: Cake Grid
cake.processingInfoUpload: Upload NPY info file (.json/.txt, auto-fills grid)

compare.title: Comparison
compare.uploadExp: Upload experimental data (.npy for cake, .tif/.edf for detector)
compare.alignHint: Flip/rotate the experimental image to align it with the simulation (stackable; click again to undo)
compare.resetAllHint: Reset the comparison display: colormap, normalization, log scale, alignment flips and experiment contrast
compare.placeholder: Upload one experiment image to compare it with the current simulation

dual.title: Dual Phase Simulation
dual.desc: Simulate a two-phase mixture by blending individual phase simulations. Set the weight fraction for each phase and independently control broadening and texture parameters.
dual.needBothPhases: Upload a peak_result.txt for both phase A and phase B.

slice.title: Slice Plots (click main image)
slice.toggleHint: Open / close the slice plots here at any time
slice.dockToolbarHint: Dock the floating slice card back inline — use this if the card was dragged off-screen and cannot be reached
slice.quickTitle: Quick Settings (applied to newly recorded peaks)
slice.quickRefineHint: Arm refine-box drawing for the selected (or last) ROI (shortcut F)

selection.title: Region Selection
selection.recordKeyHint: Records the quick settings (multiplier / background) into the new peak — shortcut R

background.title: Background
background.perPeakHint: Background subtraction is configured per peak: this panel provides the defaults for newly created peaks. Changing the fixed value syncs to every peak in fixed-value mode; each peak can still be edited individually in the ROI table below.

dbscan.applyHint: Fill the estimated background into fixed-value mode
dbscan.hint: DBSCAN clusters bright pixels into diffraction-peak clusters (red mask); every other pixel counts as background and its percentile becomes the level. Tune the parameters and re-preview until the mask matches the peaks in your image; recorded ROI regions are always treated as peaks.

saturation.title: Saturation / Bad-pixel Mask
saturation.hint: Pixels above this value (e.g. saturated/dead) are excluded from intensity extraction

roi.refineHint: Setting refine match box for ROI #{n} — drag a small box on the plot around the target Miller point.
roi.refineHintLasso: Setting refine region for ROI #{n} — circle the target Miller point with the lasso (its q/χ extremes become the match box).
roi.editingHint: Editing ROI #{n}: Record will UPDATE this row, not add a new one
roi.rowClickHint: Click to load the ROI bounds into the slice plots (edit mode: Record = update this row)

export.pngFullHint: Export the full image (unaffected by the current zoom); with the χ crop enabled, the full width over the cropped band

cake.title: NPY Files
cake.removeConfirm: Remove "{name}"? The uploaded file will be deleted from the server.
cake.removeAllConfirm: Delete all {count} uploaded image(s)? They will be removed from the server.

raw.title: Image Files
raw.placeholderHint: EDF / TIFF / H5 raw frame viewer

controls.title: Viewer Controls
controls.resetAllHint: Reset all display settings: colormap, log, colorbar, axes, reference line, q/χ ranges & crop, contrast (loaded files are kept)
controls.resetDone: Display settings restored to initial state.

export.batchByFirstHint: Export every image rendered with the first image's current display settings (pane A when comparing, otherwise the selected image)

axis.title: Axis ranges / crop
axis.hint: Import NPY info file to auto-fill the q (Å⁻¹) and χ (°) extents so the heatmap shows real physical axes instead of pixel indices.
axis.infoApplied: q / χ axis ranges applied from NPY info file
axis.infoEmpty: NPY info file contained no recognizable axis ranges

compare.toggleHint: Pick two images on the left to view side by side, each with its own contrast
compare.emptyHint: Click a file on the left to load it

cif.hklLimitDropped: hkl absolute-value limit removed {count} out-of-range peaks.

xrd.processingInfoLoaded: Applied q-χ grid from NPY info file (source unit: {unit}).

analysis.infoApplied: Applied info: {name} (image q/χ axis ranges updated).
analysis.bgEstimated: DBSCAN background estimate: level ≈ {value}, {n} peak cluster(s).
analysis.bgApplied: Applied estimated background {value} as the fixed value.

viewer.deleteMissing: {name} was not found on the server (already cleaned up); removed from the list.

cifh.title: CIF Hydrogenation
cifh.desc: Add hydrogens to refined H-free polymer structures for CP2K optimization. Polymer bonds are perceived under periodic boundaries, H fills each atom's valence, and you can inspect and fix bonds in the 3D view before exporting a Materials-Studio-style CIF.

view.title: Hydrogenated structure
view.hint: Click an atom to pick · click a bond midpoint to select · drag to rotate

edit.title: Bond editing
edit.pickHint: Click two atoms in the 3D view to bond them

export.hint: Export the H-added CIF (P1 with a _geom_bond loop and symmetry codes), ready for CP2K.

descs.basic: Minimal form needs only 5 keywords: ENABLED, DIFFRACTION_FILE, WAVELENGTH, AUTO_SCALE, LAMBDA. Absorption / density / scattering factors are auto-derived by xraylib from the cell composition + wavelength.
descs.experimental: Sample thickness and detector distance (v1.1 thickness default 0.03 cm = 0.3 mm); XRAY_MODE 0=synchrotron, 1=lab source, other=no polarization factor.
descs.hkl: hkl search range and blank penalty. Note: with MULTIPLE_UNIT_CELL supercells H_MAX / K_MAX must be scaled to supercell indices (e.g. 10 for a 2x2 supercell).
descs.bfactor: B factors are fixed and not optimized. Without a B file all atoms use B_FACTOR_DEFAULT; a B file must match the CP2K particles in order and count (supercells need supercell-length files).
descs.overrides: Explicit overrides (defaults use xraylib auto-derivation): Cromer-Mann table override, pre-generated reflection table, per-atom B file, fixed SCALE_FACTOR.
descs.output: Generate and download the &FIBER_DIFFRACTION section. String keyword values must not carry trailing inline comments (they would become part of the filename) — this generator keeps comments on their own lines.

helps.wavelength: The only energy entry [Å], E = 12.3984/WAVELENGTH keV; write the plain number, no [angstrom] unit suffix
helps.autoScale: Recommended start with .TRUE. (per-step weighted LSQ re-fit of k); disable and set SCALE_FACTOR for a fixed k
helps.scaleFactor: Only effective with AUTO_SCALE .FALSE.; take k from the zero-coupling check (LAMBDA=0 + AUTO_SCALE)
helps.lambda: Coupling strength [hartree], start small; tune linearly via the FIBER| fiber/DFT ratio (λ_new ≈ λ × target / current)
helps.hkl: Supercell note: a 2x2 supercell needs H/K_MAX = 2x the primitive values (e.g. 10); L unchanged
helps.bFactorFile: Must match the structure atoms in order and count; supercells (e.g. 2x2) need supercell-length entries
helps.overrides: Provide ATOMIC_FACTOR_FILE only for ionic systems / custom parameters; default = xraylib FF_Rayl neutral atoms
helps.atomicFactor: Cromer-Mann table (same format as refine.f90), read only as an explicit override

usage.title: Recommended workflow
usage.step1: 1) Run a zero-coupling check with LAMBDA = 0.0 + AUTO_SCALE .TRUE. and copy the auto-calibrated SCALE_FACTOR from the FIBER| LAMBDA output line;
usage.step2: 2) Fix k (AUTO_SCALE .FALSE. + SCALE_FACTOR), start GEO_OPT from a small LAMBDA, watch the FIBER| fiber/DFT ratio (0.01~0.5 is a good start);
usage.step3: 3) Do not judge λ by the R factor alone — a slight R increase can be legitimate; tune λ by the fiber/DFT force ratio.

deviation.title: Structure Deviation Report
deviation.desc: Compare a DFT-relaxed structure (CIF, or the PDB that CP2K writes) against the pre-optimisation reference: per-atom displacements under the periodic minimum image, average / RMS / maximum deviation and cell changes, with Markdown / CSV report export.

fields.matchHelp: Nearest pairs atoms by element at their closest positions (recommended — tolerates CP2K reordering); 'by file order' requires identical atom order in both files.
fields.basisHelp: Which lattice converts fractional displacements to Å — matters when the cell relaxed slightly. Default: reference cell.

result.title: Deviation Results
result.empty: Upload both structures in 'Input Structures' and click 'Compute deviations' first.

report.title: Report Export
report.hint: Render this comparison as a Markdown report (summary + cell comparison + per-atom table) or a CSV data table for archiving and further analysis.

usage.title: How to use
usage.step2: 2) Upload the DFT-relaxed structure — a CIF or the PDB written by CP2K (multi-frame trajectories use the last frame).
usage.step3: 3) Click 'Compute deviations' to inspect mean / max deviation, cell changes and the per-atom table (click headers to sort, filter by element).
usage.step4: 4) Generate and download the Markdown / CSV report under 'Report Export'.

symmetry.title: Space Group Detection
symmetry.desc: Upload a refined all-atom P1 CIF (or any symmetric CIF — it is expanded automatically). The space group is detected WITHOUT touching your cell, unlike MS/PLATON which force the structure into the standard setting and rewrite the cell. Operations are returned in the current cell basis, ready to validate a refinement.
symmetry.upload: Upload a CIF (drag & drop or click)

fields.symprecHelp: Maximum distance for positions to count as symmetry-related. Refined coordinates are only approximately symmetric — sweep the tolerance first to see how the group changes.

result.empty: Upload a CIF in “Upload & Detect” and run the detection first.
result.label: Label
result.noteHm: The H-M symbol is the standard-setting name of the group (the one MS/PLATON report); the setting matching your cell (e.g. P2₁/n) is uniquely defined by the Hall symbol and the operation list below.
result.stdRef: Standard-setting reference (the cell MS/PLATON would convert to — not applied here)
result.stdNote: Reference only: both cells describe the same lattice (|det T| ≈ 1 means it is just a change of basis/origin); no conversion is needed.
result.supercellWarn: Note: the input cell is a {n}-fold supercell of the true primitive cell; the detected operations already include the corresponding translations.

scan.title: Tolerance sweep
scan.hint: Watch how the group changes with tolerance: a group that appears already at small tolerances is trustworthy; one that only shows up at large tolerance may be pseudo-symmetry. The row of the current tolerance is highlighted.

export.hint: Both exports keep the cell parameters exactly as input: “Generate symmetrised CIF” writes the symmetry-operation loop plus asymmetric-unit atoms (Wyckoff letters included) for VESTA / Materials Studio / PLATON to expand; “Generate symmetrised P1 all-atom CIF” actually applies the symmetrisation to the coordinates (special-position atoms land exactly on their symmetry elements) and expands to a full P 1 cell for calculation programs that only read P 1.
export.hintP1: The symmetrisation has been applied to the coordinates: the largest atom displacement is shown as “Max symmetrisation shift”. The source space group is recorded as a comment inside the CIF.

usage.title: How to use
usage.step1: Upload the refined CIF and run the tolerance sweep to confirm the group is stable over a reasonable range;
usage.step2: Run the detection and check the number, H-M symbol and the operations in your own basis, making sure the maximum symmetrisation shift is small;
usage.step3: Archive or submit via the symmetrised CIF — the cell parameters are exactly those of your refinement;
usage.step4: If a calculation program needs an all-atom P 1 input, export the symmetrised P1 all-atom CIF — the symmetrisation is applied to the atoms while the cell stays untouched.
